text:
alex: Hey team — customer reported truncated SSE output from our hosted API when their Android app goes to background. Final chunk never arrives, JSON ends with a trailing comma and finish_reason is absent. Repro steps below.

maria: Can you drop their repro and any client logs? Which SDK/version?

alex: Using our Android SDK 1.4.2 (OkHttp under the hood). Repro is consistent: start streaming generation, background the app for ~5–10s, then bring it back — response often ends abruptly with no final event.

alex: Client-side capture (OkHttp event listener):
```
Event: connectionFailed
route: /v1/responses/stream
exception: EOFException: end of stream
stack: okhttp3.internal.http2.Http2Stream.getResponseHeaders
```

alex: Server-side snippet from proxy (timestamped):
```
[2026-03-16T14:12:34Z] conn=abcd1234 client=10.2.3.4 state=closed reason=RST_STREAM code=0
[2026-03-16T14:12:34Z] stream_id=17 last_event_sent=token_batch_598 trailing_bytes=7
```

sam: Does the client send a resume header on reconnect? If they resume with a mismatched byte offset we may drop the final sentinel.

alex: They do try to resume. Client sends `X-Resume-Id: abcd1234` and `X-Resume-Offset: 4096` on reconnect. Server logs show resume accepted but final event (finish_reason) never emitted for that connection id.

maria: Any indication of HTTP/2 GOAWAY or proxy-level timeouts? That could tear the stream mid-object and leave a trailing comma.

infra-bot: Attached relevant proxy events for conn=abcd1234:
```
PROXY-EVENT: STREAM_RESET id=abcd1234 code=ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM reason=stream_timed_out
PROXY-EVENT: BUFFER_FLUSH id=abcd1234 bytes_sent=8122 last_sent_segment="...,\n"
```

alex: Repro steps (condensed):
1) Start streaming response via SDK (model=gpt-ops-stream, max_tokens=1024)
2) Wait until token stream begins (client has printed ~50 tokens)
3) Press Home / background app (Android 13) for 5–15s
4) Bring app to foreground, SDK attempts automatic reconnect/resume
5) Observe truncated JSON: last characters `...,` and no `finish_reason` or final `delta` chunk.

jordan: Possible client issues: Android may pause background threads and close socket abruptly when the OS reclaims resources. OkHttp will report EOF but resume logic may replay a different offset. Two immediate mitigations: keep a foreground service while streaming or switch to short-lived heartbeat pings so server doesn't consider the stream idle.

support-engineer: Customer also reported intermittent 401 immediately after backgrounding in some sessions (auth token refresh race). Could be token refresh + resume header mismatch.

alex: Tried a local fix: on reconnect the SDK now double-checks the resume offset against server ack before replaying. Simple test reduced occurrences but did not fully eliminate them on slow devices.

sam: From runtime side, we should treat resume attempts that conflict with last_sent_segment as non-idempotent: either reject resume (force full restart) or emit explicit finalization before accepting resume. I'll open an eng-runtime ticket.

maria: For support thread — can you capture full HTTP traces (client and proxy) for one failing session and attach HAR-like dump? Also which customer (org id) so we can correlate logs and billing?

alex: Customer org: acme-mobile (org_9876). I'll attach a sample HAR and device logs. For urgency: customer impact = app shows partial assistant answers to their users ~30% of streams on Pixel 6 under heavy memory pressure.

jordan: Short term recommendation to customer: enable foreground service for live chat sessions or reduce timeouts (heartbeat every 3s). We'll follow up with an infra patch to detect resumed streams with mismatched tails and return an explicit error event so client can retry cleanly.

maria: Thanks — tagging eng-runtime and mobile SDK owners. @sam @jordan please coord on rollout and compatibility tests. :+1:

sam: I'll file PR with server-side safety: if trailing_bytes > 0 and resume_offset mismatch -> emit `{"type":"error","error":"resume_mismatch"}` then close.

alex: Adding the HAR and device logs to the ticket now. I'll keep this thread updated.
